claims.claim: Won the Women's Ballon d'Or on Monday 26 October 2026 in London, her third award
claims.note: UEFA: Monday, October 26, 2026, London; 'has won her third Women's Ballon d'Or'. Reuters: presented 'on Monday'.

claims.claim: Named ahead of Ewa Pajor and Khadija Shaw, who finished second and third
claims.note: UEFA: 'ahead of Ewa Pajor and Khadija Shaw, who finished second and third'.

claims.claim: Presented with the award on the Monday
claims.note: Reuters (via bdnews24): presented with the award 'on Monday'.

claims.claim: First two Ballon d'Or wins came in 2021 and 2022
claims.note: UEFA: 'also won in 2021 and 2022'.

claims.claim: Sky called it a record-equalling third women's Ballon d'Or
claims.note: Sky: 'claimed a record-equalling third women's Ballon d'Or'. Sky does not name the player.

claims.claim: Won while playing for London City Lionesses
claims.note: Reuters photo caption identifies her as a London City Lionesses player; Sky text covers the London City move. The Sky video page returned 404 and is not cited in the new text.

claims.claim: Record she equals is Aitana Bonmatí's, three awards
claims.note: 101 Great Goals: 'She equals her former team-mate Bonmati's record of three awards.'

claims.claim: Since her July move: three goals and one assist in seven WSL games
claims.note: Sky: 'scored three goals and has an assist in her seven WSL games'.

claims.claim: Reuters says Barcelona won the treble in 2025-26; Sky and 101 Great Goals say quadruple
claims.note: Reuters: 'won the treble with Barcelona in the 2025-26 campaign'. Sky: 'captained Barcelona to a quadruple last season'. 101 GG: 'continental quadruple in 2025-26'.

claims.claim: Left FC Barcelona in May 2026 after 14 seasons; departure announced Tuesday 26 May 2026
claims.note: AP: announced Tuesday May 26, 2026; 14 seasons.

claims.claim: Joined Barcelona in 2012 at 18, from Levante
claims.note: AP: joined from Levante in 2012 at 18.

claims.claim: 507 games (second on the all-time list), 232 goals (club record), 38 trophies, four Champions Leagues, ten Spanish league titles
claims.note: AP article figures match.

claims.claim: Fourth Champions League title won on Saturday, 'fourth time in six seasons'
claims.note: AP: 'on Saturday helped Barcelona win the Champions League title for the fourth time in six seasons'.

claims.claim: Farewell article calls the win a determining moment in her decision to leave
claims.note: FC Barcelona: she recognised lifting the fourth Champions League trophy was a determining moment. The page does not say the trophy was lifted by her in other words; the new text does not claim it.

claims.claim: Club calls her its first women's Ballon d'Or winner (2021); 2020 cancelled because of Covid-19; record two wins; first two-time winner in consecutive years
claims.note: FC Barcelona 2022 article: first-ever winner for the club, 2020 cancelled for Covid-19, record two wins, first two-time winner in consecutive years.

claims.claim: Quotes from 2022 club report: 'when I won a year ago I told myself I had to get even better and serve the team'; 'I'm proud to play for Barça, my lifetime club'
claims.note: Both quotes confirmed verbatim in the club article.

claims.claim: Departure video: 'The time has come to acknowledge that I've given everything for these colors'; described her time at the club as 'a perfect story'
claims.note: AP quotes the video line and 'It's been a perfect story'.

claims.claim: Farewell at Camp Nou on the Wednesday after the announcement; more than 91,000 people chanted her name
claims.note: FC Barcelona: farewell on a Wednesday; 'more than 91,000 people would chant her name'.

claims.claim: Said she felt 'an incredible emptiness' the day before and was 'full of love' on the day
claims.note: FC Barcelona: 'Yesterday my heart hurt. I felt an incredible emptiness. Today I am full of love.'

claims.claim: Xavi Llorens brought her back and said she had no ceiling as a player or person
claims.note: FC Barcelona: 'She did not have a ceiling as a player nor as a person.'

claims.claim: Video tribute with messages from Puyol, Busquets, Iniesta, Pedri, Raphinha and former teammates; song 'Magnolias'; ended with photograph and collective hug
claims.note: FC Barcelona lists these names, former players, 'Magnolias' and the photo and hug.

claims.claim: Vicky López called her 'an example on and off the field'; academy for more than 400 girls with the FC Barcelona Foundation
claims.note: FC Barcelona: 'She is an example on and off the field'; academy for more than 400 girls.

claims.claim: Club describes her as making Barcelona 'a world leader in women's football' and her career 'changed the face of women's football'
claims.note: Club's own wording, attributed as such in the text.

claims.claim: Born 4 February 1994 in Mollet del Vallès; Spanish; attacking midfield
claims.note: SoccerDonna: 04.02.1994; Mollet del Vallés; Spain; attacking midfield.

claims.claim: World Cup winner with Spain; part of the 2023 World Cup squad
claims.note: AP: 'a World Cup winner with Spain'. Al Jazeera: part of Spain's 2023 World Cup-winning squad.

claims.claim: Named the world's best female player in 2021 and 2022
claims.note: Al Jazeera: 'crowned the world's best female player in 2021 and 2022'.

claims.claim: Signed for London City Lionesses; announced Wednesday 8 July 2026 as a 'statement signing'; aged 32
claims.note: AP: Wednesday, July 8, 2026, 'statement signing', age 32. Al Jazeera: 32-year-old.

claims.claim: Three-year deal
claims.note: CBS: 'three-year contract'.

claims.claim: Barcelona contract expired at the end of June 2026
claims.note: AP: contract expired at the end of June 2026.

claims.claim: Said she wanted to change and challenge herself
claims.note: CBS quote: 'I want to change, I want to improve, I want to challenge myself'.

claims.claim: CBS mentions a salary figure, which this page does not repeat
claims.note: CBS article mentions a salary figure; the page does not repeat it and makes no claim about its status.

claims.claim: London City owned by Michele Kang, who also owns OL Lyonnes; promoted in 2025; sixth of 12 in first season
claims.note: AP: Kang owns the club and OL Lyonnes; promoted 2025; sixth of 12.

claims.claim: Putellas quotes on ambition, impact; Kang quote on pinnacle of talent
claims.note: AP quotes match verbatim.

claims.claim: Summary and FAQ: equals Aitana Bonmatí's record of three awards
claims.note: 101 Great Goals states the record; Sky states 'record-equalling'.

valueNote: Adds the 26 October 2026 result from UEFA's report, the record-equalling detail with the Barcelona season conflict between Reuters and Sky, and WSL form since the July move. These are not in the usual top results at this detail.
summary: All claims in the English page match the cited sources. The new October 2026 section uses UEFA for the result, Sky and 101 Great Goals for the record and WSL form, and flags the conflict between Reuters (treble) and Sky/101 Great Goals (quadruple) without choosing a number.
